```{r}
library(tidyverse)
#import data
ielts <- read_csv(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2026/2026-08-18/demo_by_first_language.csv"
)
#data cleaning
glimpse(ielts)
ielts_clean <- ielts |>
  filter(
    !is.na(language),
    !is.na(band),
    !is.na(percent),
    !is.na(type)
  )
glimpse(ielts_clean)
```
```{r}
head(ielts)
str(ielts)
```
**1. RQ1: What is the overall distribution of IELTS scores?**
```{r}
# Bar chart
ielts_clean |>
  group_by(band) |>
  summarise(avg_percent = mean(percent)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = band, y = avg_percent)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of IELTS Scores",
    x = "IELTS Band",
    y = "Average Percentage"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
**Research Question 1 Findings**
::: {.callout-tip title="Score distribution"}
The distribution of IELTS scores is slightly skewed to the left, with the highest average percentages occurring at bands 6.0 and 6.5 (around 18%). Most scores are concentrated between 5.5 and 7.5, while extremely low and high scores are relatively uncommon. The average percentage gradually increases from lower bands, peaks at 6.0–6.5, and then decreases toward higher bands. Overall, the results suggest that intermediate IELTS band levels are more common than extreme scores across the groups represented in the dataset.
:::
